title: The Twelve Disciples
description: Fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot, a doubter and a traitor: the twelve ordinary men Jesus chose to change the world. Simon Peter, Andrew, James and John, Matthew, Thomas, Philip and Nathanael, the quiet ones whose names we barely know, and Judas. Who they were, how Jesus shaped them, and what their stories mean for us, from the King James Bible, with a closing prayer.

beats.say: He went up into a mountain, and called unto him whom he would. And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach.
Notice the order. First, that they should be with him. Only then, that he might send them. Before they did anything for him, they spent three years simply walking with him.
No priests, no scholars, no one important. Fishermen, a tax collector, a revolutionary. If he could build his church on them, he can do something with you.
Simon was a fisherman from Bethsaida: loud, impulsive, always first to speak. Jesus gave him a new name before he had earned it: Peter, the rock.
He walked on water, and sank. He declared, Thou art the Christ, and minutes later tried to talk Jesus out of the cross. Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.
On the worst night of his life, by a fire in a courtyard, he denied knowing Jesus three times. And the cock crew. And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
After the resurrection, by another fire, on a beach, Jesus asked him three times: Lovest thou me? Three denials, three chances. Feed my lambs. Feed my sheep.
The man who failed loudest became the rock after all. Jesus does not choose people because they will not fall. He chooses them, and then he restores them.
Andrew heard John the Baptist say, Behold the Lamb of God, and followed Jesus home. And the first thing he did: He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias.
And he brought him to Jesus. Andrew is mentioned only a handful of times, and almost every time, he is bringing someone to Jesus.

His brother, a boy with five loaves, a group of Greeks who wanted to see Jesus. Never the famous one. Always the one who introduced people. Some of the most important work in the kingdom looks like that.
James and John were mending nets with their father Zebedee when Jesus called. He surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder. It was not a compliment.
When a Samaritan village refused them, they asked: Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them? But he turned, and rebuked them.

They asked for the best seats in his glory, one on his right hand, the other on his left. And Jesus said: whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.
James became the first of the twelve to die for him. John lived to be an old man and wrote three words that summed up everything he had learned: God is love. Thunder, turned into love.
Jesus saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom: a tax collector, working for Rome, getting rich off his own people. Every devout Jew in Capernaum despised him.
And he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him. A fisherman could go back to his boat. A tax collector who walked away from his booth could never go back.
He threw a party for his old friends to meet Jesus. And the man who used to keep careful records of other people's money wrote the first book of the New Testament.
Matthew wrote for his own people, showing them again and again that Jesus fulfilled their scriptures. The man they had called a traitor spent his life telling them good news.
We call him doubting Thomas. But when Jesus decided to go back to Judea, where they had tried to stone him, Thomas said: Let us also go, that we may die with him.
He was the one who asked the honest question: Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way? And got the answer: I am the way.

He missed the first appearance of the risen Lord, and would not take anyone's word for it: Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.
Eight days later Jesus came again, and went straight to him: Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered, My Lord and my God.
Jesus did not shame his doubt. He met it. Then he spoke of us: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed. Bring him your honest questions. He comes to doubters.
Philip found his friend Nathanael: We have found him, Jesus of Nazareth. Nathanael scoffed: Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.
Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee. And Nathanael said: Rabbi, thou art the Son of God.

Three years later Philip still had one request: Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us. Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father.
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James. Names we barely know, men who did their work without headlines.
Simon the Zealot belonged to a movement that wanted to drive Rome out by force. Matthew had worked for Rome. Jesus put them in the same small group, and asked them to love one another.
The church has always been like this: people who would never have chosen each other, chosen by the same Lord. If he can make a family of a zealot and a tax collector, he can make one of us.
Judas was trusted with the money bag. John tells us plainly: he was a thief, and had the bag. He walked with Jesus for three years, saw every miracle, and was never truly changed.
He went to the chief priests: What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver. The price of a slave.
At supper Jesus said one of them would betray him. Judas asked: Master, is it I? He said unto him, Thou hast said. And still Jesus washed his feet, and still called him friend in the garden.

Afterward Judas brought the silver back: I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. Peter and Judas both failed him that night. One came back to Jesus. One did not. The difference was not the sin. It was the return.
He called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two. Never alone. Even the apostles needed a companion on the road.
Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead: freely ye have received, freely give. No bag, no bread, no money in their purse. They had to trust him for everything.
Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves. Clear-eyed about the world, and gentle in it.
On the road to Capernaum, the twelve argued behind his back. When he asked what they had been discussing, they held their peace: for they had disputed among themselves, who should be the greatest.
He sat down, called the twelve, and said: If any man desire to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all.
And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them, and took him in his arms. Greatness in his kingdom looks like making room for the smallest person in the room.
Fifty days after the resurrection, the disciples were gathered in one place in Jerusalem, waiting, as he had told them. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind.
And Peter, the man who weeks earlier could not admit to a servant girl that he knew Jesus, stood up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and preached to the whole city.
Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins. And the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls.
The coward became the preacher. Not because Peter tried harder, but because the Spirit came. What God asks of you, he also gives you the power to do.
After Pentecost these same men stood before the council that had condemned Jesus. They spoke with such boldness that the rulers marvelled, for they were unlearned and ignorant men.
And they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus. No degree, no rank, no money. Only that one thing, and it was enough.
Within a generation their enemies complained: These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also. Eleven ordinary men, and a world turned upside down.
Let us pray. Lord Jesus, you chose fishermen and tax collectors, doubters and hotheads. Thank you that you chose me too, as I am, not as I pretend to be.
When I am loud like Peter and fall like Peter, restore me like Peter. When I am quiet like Andrew, use me to bring someone to you.
When I doubt like Thomas, show me your hands. When I want to be the greatest, put a child in my arms. And whenever I fail, do not let me walk away like Judas. Bring me back.
Let people see in me that I have been with Jesus. Follow me, you said. I will. Amen.
